MAGLANGIT Barangay Treasurer Barangay Cogon, Balingasag Misamis Oriental Dear Ms. Llona and Ms. Maglangit: 03 JUL 2017 This has reference to your letter dated 08 June 2017, which was forwarded to the Central Office by DILG-Region X Director Arnel M. Agabe in a 1st Indorsement, which we received on 20 June 201. In your aforesaid letter, you are seeking the Department's opinion on the following issues which we quoted in tota I. 2. 3. 4. 5. Is there a vacancy of Robert Valmores' office? Is there a need to change the signatories Of the bank account of the barangay funds this early? Is there a need for the immediate change of the barangay treasurer and barangay secretary? Has the presumption of innocence of Robert Valmores been abandoned by any law of jurisprudence? Is Robert Valmores' elective position considered vacant, him being in currently in jail while the case against him is still pending? Your above-enumerated queries were prompted by the following facts: Punong Barangay Robert Valmores of Barangay Cogon was arrested for allegedly in possession of dangerous drugs punishable under RA 9165 or the Dangerous Drugs Act; Some members of the Sangguniang Barangay who are politically opposed to PB Valmores declared the latter's position vacant;

Others are of the belief that PB Valmores should still be presumed innocent unless proven otherwise; • PB Valmores still performs his functions and gives instruction that the Officer- in-Charge should be rotated among the barangay officials every week; • However, some members of the sangguniang barangay still insists that PB Valmores shall be considered vacant and a new Punong Barangay be appointed. Since your first, fourth and fifth queries are related, we shall answer them in one (1) discussion. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 22, series of 2014, the Department, citing the cases of People of the Philippines vs. Jalosjosa clarified that the confinement at the National Bilibid Prison of a Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, an elective official just like herein PB Valmores, should not be construed as removal from his position unless otherwise disqualified. In the same opinion, the Department further clarified that such confinement however prevents the accused elective official from performing his duties and functions as Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member. As a legal basis thereto, the Department cited the case of People of the Philippines vs. Maceda, et aP where the Supreme Court held: "As a matter of law, when a person indicted Tor an offense is arrested, he is deemed placed under the custody of the law. He is placed in actual restraint of' liberty in jail so that he may be bound to answer for the commission of the offense. He must be detained in jail during the pendency of the case against him, unless he is authorized by the court to be released on bail oron recognizance. let it be stressed that allprisoners whether under preventive detention or serving final sentence can not practice their profession nor engage in any business or occupation, or hold office. elective or appointive. while in detention. This is a necessary consequence of arrest and detention. Consequently, all the accused in Criminal Cases Nos. 3350- 3355 must be confined in the Provincial jail of Antique. " (Emphasis Supplied) Since the accused elective official is prevented from performing his duties and functions as Sangguniang Panlalawigan Member, we considered such incident in DILG Legal Opinion No. 22, series of 2014 as a temporary incapacity due to physical or legal G.R. No. 132875-76 dated 03 February 2000. G.R. No. 89591-96, 24 January 2000.

reasons, which shall thereafter give rise to a temporary vacancy in his office per Section 46 (a)3 of the Local Government Code of 1991. It bears stressing that the aforesaid Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 does not limit the grounds for temporary incapacity in the office of the local chief executive to those enumerated therein, such as leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. The grounds are not exclusive. Said provision uses the phrase "such as, but not limited to" which only implies other similar cases. There being a temporary vacancy in the office of the Punong Barangay, applying Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the Punong Barangay, until the temporary incapacity of PB Valmores subsists. As to your second query, we note that under Section 3444 of the Local Government Code of 1991, the local chief executive himself is required whenever local funds are disbursed. However, in case of his temporary absence or incapacity, the same provision states that the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor. As to your third query on the need for the immediate change of the barangay treasurer and barangay secretary, may we invite your attention to Section I, Article II of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-1505, thus: SECTION I. Fxcept in cases ofdisbursements involving regularly recurring adm inistrative expenws such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to government creditor agencies such as GSIS, SSS, LBP, DBP, National Printing Office, Prcx:urement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed. In cases of special or trust funds, disbursements shall be approved by the administrator of the fund. In case of temporary absence or incapacity of the departrnent head or chief of office, the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor. 5 Entitled "GUIDELINES ON THE APPOINTMENT OF BARANGAY SECRETARIES, TREASURERS AND OTHER APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS"

terminus with the appointing authority (CSC Opinion dated 28 July 1998, addressed to then Director Almario M. de los Santos, Legal Service, DILG). As could be gleaned from the foregoing, this Department made as basis Civil Service Commission opinion dated 28 July 1998 addressed to then Director Almario M. de los Santos, Legal Service of this Department. In that opinion, the Civil Service Commission ruled that by their nature, the appointment of Barangay Secretaries, Barangay Treasurers and other barangay appointive officials are either co-terminus with the appointing authority or co-existent with the tenure of the appointing authority, or at his pleasure. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 19, series of 2006, the Department opined: xxx upon the death of the Punong Barangay, the term of office of the Barangay Secretary, Barangay Treasurer and other barangay appointive officials whose appointments are coterminus with him being the appointing authority shall likewise expire. This is a case of expiration of term of office, and not removal, of this kind of officials where concurrence by majority of the Members of the Sangguniang Barangay is not anymore required. It is only in case of removal where such concurrence is required by law and jurisprudence. We hope to have guided you on the matter. 1.8/17 Copy furnished: DIR. ARNEL M.
